posts.text: Materialize prices a 3D print from the repaired mesh: it measures the true solid volume and charges that volume in your material, paid in USDC on Solana: three.ws/materialize

media.alt: The three.ws Materialize page: a drop area for any .glb beside models fresh from the Forge, over three columns explaining that the price is measured from the repaired mesh, that checkout is USDC on Solana, and that agents can order over x402.

claims.says: measures the true solid volume and charges that volume in your material

evidence.contains: Every quote comes from the mesh itself: the analyzer computes the true solid volume of the repaired model, and the price is that volume in the material you picked. Nothing is estimated from a bounding box.
There is no card processor. You pay the exact quoted amount in USDC on Solana, the order is opened against a signed quote, and the price can never move between the quote and the charge.

posts.text:
Put a living 3D agent on your website in 30 seconds.

Two lines of HTML. No build step, no npm install.

Paste, refresh, and a 3D character is standing in the corner of your page, greeting visitors and answering questions.

As easy as embedding a video.

three.ws/tutorials/embed-in-30-seconds

media.alt: A three.ws card reading 'A 3D agent on your website. Two lines.' above the two HTML tags that do it, beside a browser window showing a bookshop's site with a 3D character standing in the bottom corner offering to say hi

posts.text:
How it works:

Build your agent at three.ws/create. Pick a character, give it a name and a personality.

Copy its ID into the two lines, and refresh your page.

It animates, greets and chats out of the box. Works in plain HTML, React and Next.js.

evidence.contains: One script tag, one `<agent-3d>` tag, one working 3D agent.

claims.says: No build step, no npm install

evidence.contains: No build step, no npm install, no framework adapter

It animates, greets and chats out of the box
